statement: For X uniform on [-1,1] and the scalar H_X=X, the unit-vector spectral measure is delta_X for every realization, yet sup over E in R and eta>0 of E[Im(X-E-i eta)^(-1)/pi] is at most 1/2. Therefore this annealed first-moment bound alone does not imply almost-sure absolute continuity.
assumptions: Scalar self-adjoint random operator on C

statement: For a measurable probability-measure kernel mu_omega on R on a standard probability space, a bounded open I, and f_eta=P_eta*mu_omega, almost-sure absolute continuity on I is equivalent to local uniform integrability of f_eta in L1(P x Lebesgue): for every closed positive-length J compactly contained in I, lim_M sup_0<eta<1 E integral_J f_eta 1_{f_eta>M}=0.
proof_or_counterexample: Full draft proof in INDEPENDENT.md: joint weak L1 compactness, event-weighted tests and a countable dense test family for sufficiency; joint density and approximate identity for necessity.
remaining_gap: Independent proof check pending; no joint uniform-integrability estimate established for the fixed-disorder Z^3 Anderson model.

statement: DRAFT, independent review pending. The density g(E)=1/[E(log(1/E))^2] on (0,exp(-1)), zero elsewhere, integrates to one and lies in no Lp for p>1. Multiplication by E on L2(g(E)dE) is a bounded self-adjoint operator whose unit-vector spectral measure is g(E)dE. Its normalized Poisson densities converge in L1 and are uniformly integrable, but their pth energy moments diverge as eta tends to zero for every p>1 on any interval containing the support in its interior. Thus a higher-moment sufficient condition is stronger than spectral absolute continuity; failure to prove it is not a refutation of the Anderson conjecture.
proof_or_counterexample: Substitute u=log(1/E): mass integral equals integral_1^infinity u^-2=1, while the pth norm integral is integral_1^infinity exp((p-1)u)u^-2p=infinity. L1 Poisson convergence yields UI; Fatou excludes uniform higher moments.
remaining_gap: Independent check pending; not an Anderson-model theorem
